questions.q: Which is a characteristic of monopolistic competition?
options: Differentiated products and low barriers to entry
questions.why: Many firms, a little different from each other, and easy entry.

questions.q: Why does a firm in monopolistic competition face a downward-sloping demand curve?
options: Its product is a little different, so it keeps some customers if it raises its price
questions.why: Differentiation means a price rise loses some customers, not all of them.

questions.q: In long-run equilibrium a firm in monopolistic competition produces at the lowest point of ATC.
questions.why: It produces to the left of the lowest point, so it has excess capacity.

questions.q: New firms enter a monopolistically competitive market. What happens to demand for an existing firm?
options: It shifts left and becomes more elastic
It shifts right and becomes less elastic
questions.why: Customers are shared with more firms, and there are more substitutes.

questions.q: Match each action by a café to the type of competition.
pairs: A 20p cut in the price of coffee
A lunch deal at a lower price
questions.why: Non-price competition wins customers without lowering the price.

questions.q: Explain why firms in monopolistic competition are not productively efficient in the long run.

ideas.label: AR slopes down, so it touches ATC to the left of ATC's lowest point
So the firm has excess capacity: more output would lower average cost

questions.model: The demand curve slopes down, so it touches ATC to the left of ATC's lowest point. The firm has excess capacity, because making more would lower its average cost.
questions.why: Productive efficiency needs the lowest point of ATC.

tests.answer: The demand curve slopes down so it touches ATC to the left of the lowest point, which means the firm has excess capacity.
